transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net advanced technical support, my name is Zoe. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Zoe. I'm hoping you can help with a network routing issue. I have a Synology NAS server at home for my photography business, but ever since our connection was upgraded to the new Fibre 500 tier on Monday, my external DDNS hostname and port forwarding have completely stopped working from outside my home network.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you troubleshoot external DDNS and port forwarding access. First, could you confirm your full name and the installation address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Kieran Gallagher, 18 Waverley Gardens, Edinburgh, EH4 3PJ.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Kieran. Having self-hosted storage inaccessible when you run a business is definitely a major inconvenience, so let's check your WAN IP configuration immediately. And what is the four-digit security PIN on the account, Kieran?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Kieran, verification is complete. So what I understand is you have a Synology NAS that was previously reachable externally via DDNS, but following the Fibre 500 upgrade, incoming port forwarding has stopped functioning from outside your local network, is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. I can access DSM locally on 192.168.1.50, but my Synology dot me hostname times out completely when connecting from 5G or client offices.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What WAN IP address is currently displayed on the broadband status page of your Hub router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: In the Hub router status, the WAN IPv4 address starts with 100.64.42.18.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That explains the issue immediately. An IP address in the one hundred dot sixty-four block indicates your connection is provisioned behind Carrier-Grade NAT, or CGNAT.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Aha! That's why! CGNAT means I don't have a unique public IPv4 address, so incoming NAT port forwarding packets have nowhere to route!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly. S-Net utilizes CGNAT by default across new residential full fibre deployments to conserve IPv4 address space, but we provide a free public IPv4 opt-out for customers hosting servers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you opt my connection out of CGNAT so I get a standard dynamic public IPv4 address?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. I will take direct ownership of updating your RADIUS subscriber profile right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does opting out cost anything extra on my monthly bill?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, opting out of CGNAT is completely free of charge on all Fibre 500 and Fibre 900 tiers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's fantastic. How long does the IP reassignment take?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously the PPP session will terminate briefly when I toggle the RADIUS flag, dropping the connection for about twenty seconds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am ready for the drop, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we are on your router settings, did you also configure IPv6 prefix delegation for your local network?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the Hub is receiving a slash fifty-six delegated prefix.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That gives every device on your LAN a globally routable IPv6 address alongside your public IPv4.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I have AAAA records set up in Cloudflare as well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That provides dual-stack redundancy if you ever connect from IPv6-only cellular networks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Very useful when travelling overseas.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, why can't S-Net just assign business users a static IPv4 address? Can you provision a static IP for me right now without extra fees?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand that having a permanent static IP would make hosting simpler for your photography business, Kieran, but unfortunately our residential Fibre 500 package does not include free static IPs and I cannot assign one without a business contract tariff; however, dynamic public IP combined with your Synology DDNS provides identical functionality at zero extra cost.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fair enough Zoe, as long as dynamic public IP works with DDNS without CGNAT, that's completely acceptable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you don't have any MTU clamping issues on port 5001?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, standard fifteen-hundred-byte MTU runs cleanly across the line.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And your upstream bandwidth is testing at full one hundred megabits?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, upload speed test shows ninety-eight megabits sustained.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That ensures fast photo gallery transfers for your photography clients.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, high upload speed is the main reason I upgraded to Fibre 500.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And your contract includes our twenty-four-seven business priority fault desk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good to know I have priority support if anything ever drops.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Toggling CGNAT opt-out flag on the subscriber database now. Bear with me for forty seconds while the session renegotiates.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Kieran. The broadband session has reconnected.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The broadband light on my router is solid green again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Refresh the router status page on your computer. What is your new WAN IP address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Refreshing... The WAN IP address is now 82.35.194.88! A real public IP address!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just confirming before we test remote access, your Synology is using local IP 192.168.1.50, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, static reservation at 192.168.1.50.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now test updating your DDNS hostname inside Synology DSM.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Clicking 'Update Now' in DSM External Access... Green status indicator! 'DDNS status: Normal. External IP: 82.35.194.88'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now disconnect your phone from home Wi-Fi, turn on 5G mobile data, and try accessing your Synology URL.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wi-Fi turned off on phone, on cellular data... Loading my Synology URL on port 5001... DSM login screen loaded instantly over 5G!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Can you log in and confirm file browsing and Photo Station are responsive?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Logged in, opening Photo Station... Full raw photo galleries loading smoothly! Remote client access is completely restored!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms two-way port forwarding and public DNS routing are working with zero CGNAT encapsulation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You have resolved this so quickly Zoe. I was dreading having to explain CGNAT to a first-line script reader, and you fixed it in ten minutes!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm your billing contact email on file, it's kieran dot gallagher at scotphoto dot com, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that's my business email.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will ensure the CGNAT opt-out tag is permanently saved to your account profile so it persists through future firmware updates.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Zoe, that's very reassuring.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm for the account profile, the installation postcode is EH4 3PJ, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, EH4 3PJ.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else with your Fibre 500 service that I can assist you with today, Kieran?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Zoe, the speed is phenomenal and remote access is back. Thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my absolute pleasure. Thank you for choosing S-Net, Kieran, and have a wonderful day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Zoe, goodbye.
